page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-64 is a compute-dense instance configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated virtual CPUs via two threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory is configured at 64 GB, presenting a lean 1 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage for non-volatile filesystems. Architectural instruction support features AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but excludes AVX-512 instruction extensions.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational capabilities across multi-threaded operations. The instance scores in the top 25% of evaluated systems in stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, as well as in PassMark overall CPU, extended instructions, encryption, and physics calculations. Real-world computational tasks such as Geekbench ray tracing and image processing similarly attain top-quartile performance, alongside small-model LLM generation speeds reaching 291.77 tokens per second. In contrast, uncached memory bandwidth performance is average, delivering 132.04 GB/sec read and 59.49 GB/sec write speeds on 256 MB blocks, while software compilation and decompression rates remain in the middle 50% tier.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the high vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes raw arithmetic throughput without incurring costs for unneeded memory capacity. The primary technical tradeoff is the limited memory footprint per thread, which restricts suitability for large in-memory databases or datasets that cannot fit comfortably within 64 GB. The absence of local solid-state drives also places I/O throughput dependencies on remote persistent disks. Consequently, this server profile is best suited for compute-intensive batch processing, video transcoding, continuous integration build jobs, image rendering pipelines, and CPU-bound microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-64 is a compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs, accompanied by 64 GB of system RAM, yielding a lean 1 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage or GPUs, requiring attached storage solutions for persistent data. Hardware capabilities include accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instructions, along with AVX support. In performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing power, excelling in stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU suites, ray tracing, and image processing. However, uncached memory bandwidth and compiler workloads remain within median industry tiers. With an emphasis on core count over memory density, n2d-highcpu-64 provides strong compute-per-resource efficiency for parallel compute workloads, batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, media transcoding, and lightweight CPU inference.
